title: Life-inspired interoceptive artificial intelligence for autonomous and adaptive agents - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Nature Machine Intelligence Perspective (Lee, Oh et al., with Karl Friston) argues that interoception — the biological monitoring and regulation of internal states to maintain homeostasis — is a missing ingredient for building AI agents with genuine adaptive autonomy, and proposes a mathematical framework plus the EVAAA virtual benchmark for implementing it. Note: only the abstract, figure captions, references and author/funding metadata are available in this record; the full body is behind Springer Nature's subscription wall despite the record being flagged non-paywalled.

themes.theme: Interoception as the missing layer for AI autonomy

insights.claim: Despite remarkable advances in AI (large language models, deep RL, diffusion models), building agents that can autonomously pursue goals while adapting to continuously changing environments remains a fundamental unsolved challenge.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Signals that leading researchers see current scaling-era AI as structurally short of true autonomy — a gap that new architectural paradigms (not just bigger models) would need to fill.
insights.quote: building agents that can autonomously pursue goals while adapting to continuously changing environments remains a fundamental challenge

insights.claim: Interoception — the process of monitoring and regulating internal bodily states to maintain homeostasis, which underwrites an organism's survival — is proposed as the biological blueprint for giving artificial agents adaptive autonomy.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Watch for 'interoceptive AI' / homeostatic-agent architectures as a research vector in embodied AI and robotics, distinct from LLM scaling.
insights.quote: interoception—the process of monitoring and regulating internal bodily states to maintain internal homeostasis—which underwrites an organism’s survival

insights.claim: The proposed unified account integrates cybernetics (Wiener, Ashby) with recent theories of life, reinforcement learning and neuroscience — reviving 1940s-60s control-theoretic ideas as a foundation for modern agent design.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A cybernetics revival in top-tier AI venues suggests the field is looking pre-deep-learning for autonomy principles; relevant to robotics and safety-critical autonomous systems R&D roadmaps.
insights.quote: integrating insights from cybernetics with recent advances in theories of life, reinforcement learning and neuroscience

insights.claim: Building interoceptive AI requires explicitly factorizing state variables into internal versus external environments and mathematically formalizing life-inspired properties that govern internal-state dynamics — abstracting internal states away from their biological instantiation.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Concrete design recipe: agent architectures that separate self-monitoring state from world-model state; a differentiator to look for in next-gen robotics/agent stacks.
insights.quote: This requires explicit factorization of state variables representing internal and external environments, together with mathematical formalization of life-inspired properties governing internal-state dynamics.

insights.claim: Internal states can serve as universally available and intrinsically valuable contexts — stable reference signals that modulate learning and behaviour even as external environments change — offering a potential fix for non-stationarity and continual-learning failures in RL.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: If internal homeostatic variables can anchor reward and learning, this addresses reward-specification and distribution-shift problems that currently limit deployed autonomous systems.
insights.quote: internal states can also function as universally available and intrinsically valuable contexts, serving as stable reference signals that modulate learning and behaviour under changing external environments

insights.claim: Biological neuromodulatory mechanisms (e.g., dopamine/serotonin-like gain control) can be incorporated into artificial agents to support context-dependent adaptive behaviour, drawing on prior work showing neuromodulation can mitigate catastrophic forgetting in neural networks.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Neuromodulation-inspired meta-learning is a named mechanism to watch in lifelong-learning-machine research and neuromorphic computing.
insights.quote: interoception-related biological processes, such as neuromodulatory mechanisms, can be incorporated to support context-dependent adaptive behaviour

insights.claim: The authors point to EVAAA, a virtual environment platform for 'essential variables' in autonomous and adaptive agents (published at NeurIPS/Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems Vol. 38), as a concrete benchmark for implementing interoceptive AI.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A named, citable benchmark gives this research program a measurable footing — benchmark adoption is the leading indicator of whether interoceptive AI gains traction.
insights.quote: Overview of the EVAAA benchmark for implementing interoceptive AI.

insights.claim: The Perspective is co-authored by Karl J. Friston (UCL, free-energy principle originator, Wellcome Trust-funded) with a Korean team at the Institute for Basic Science and Sungkyunkwan University, backed by Korean government grants (IBS, NRF, IITP 'Human Cognition-Based AI Core Technology') — indicating state-funded Korean investment in biologically inspired AI.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: South Korea's MSIT is funding cognition-based AI core technology as a national program; a policy/funding thread worth tracking for non-US AI research bets.
insights.quote: Development of Human Cognition-Based AI Core Technology

insights.claim: One co-author (Hyebhin Yoon) is affiliated with Neurocore Co. Ltd, a Seoul company, and the team operates a 'Life-inspired Neural Network for Prediction and Optimization Research Group' — early evidence of commercial translation of interoceptive/homeostatic AI concepts in Korea.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Flags a private-company vehicle attached to this research line; a name to watch if life-inspired agent architectures move from journals to products.
insights.locator: Neurocore Co. Ltd, Seoul, South Korea

insights.claim: The reference list ties interoceptive AI to the AI-consciousness debate, citing Bengio & Elmoznino's 'Illusions of AI consciousness' (Science, 2025) and Butlin et al.'s consciousness-indicator work — placing body-based internal-state models at the center of that emerging controversy.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Interoceptive architectures may become the technical battleground for AI-consciousness and machine-welfare debates, with regulatory and reputational implications for AI labs.
